# Occasion and audience

## What this deck is made for

- Occasion: a training once the first controls are running and measuring is due
- Audience: `practitioners`
- Length: 45 minutes, with a shared exercise at the end
- What the listeners already know: the objectives from ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.2,
  and which controls came out of the risk treatment

::: {.notes}
This slide is not presented. The deck for the leadership sits beside it and
answers a different question, namely which measures get put forward at all.
This one shows the build of a single one.
:::

# What it is about

## The subject in one sentence

ISO/IEC 27004 says how you get from a running control to a number somebody can
read something off and decide on.

## Four words, four activities

- Monitoring: establishing what state something is in
- Measuring: assigning it a value
- Analysing: forming a connection out of several values
- Evaluating: reading the result off a yardstick set beforehand
- Anyone doing only the second has numbers and no statement
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 9.1

# The four questions before the first count

## The build

- Which objective from 6.2 is the measure meant to evidence
- What gets counted directly, and where does it arise
- How does the calculation run
- Above which value does what happen, and who decides that

The fourth is usually missing. Without it a number arises that gets
renegotiated in every meeting.

## Two rules for the second question

- Counting runs from sources that exist anyway
- A measure needing something collected specially for it stops being collected
  after two quarters

# An example, worked through

## The objective and the count

- Objective: no access stays in place longer than ten working days after a
  change of role
- What gets counted: the changes of role per quarter, and per change the
  working days until the withdrawal
- What gets calculated: the share of changes where the withdrawal happened
  within ten working days
- Threshold: below 90 per cent it gets put forward and one further control gets
  named

## Two quarters

| Quarter | Changes | of those in time | Share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q3 | 4 | 3 | 75 per cent |
| Q4 | 6 | 5 | 83 per cent |

The value rose and still lies below the threshold. The action follows from the
threshold and not from the direction.

## Why the base stands beside it

- Three out of four is 75 per cent, thirty out of forty is too
- A share without its base is the commonest mistake in a paper
- The numbers are invented and come from no real organisation

# What to do or decide afterwards

## The next steps

- Answer the four questions for a control that is already running, and write
  them down
- Fix the threshold before counting for the first time
- Collect twice before anything gets put forward
- Write it down even when there was nothing to do
- After four quarters, decide whether the measure stays

# References

## Standard, clause and edition

- ISO/IEC 27004:2016, as a whole standard
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.2
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 10.1
- ISO/IEC 27002:2022, 5.15, as an example of the form of a reference

No text from a standard stands on these slides. No clause number of
ISO/IEC 27004 is named, and the reason stands in the chapter on that standard.
The three levels of a measure are named here in our own words and therefore do
not carry the terms the standard uses for them.
